title: Garry Winogrand

publisher.name: San Francisco Museum of Modern Art / Yale University Press

description.main: Catalogue of the SFMOMA and National Gallery of Art Winogrand retrospective, edited by Leo Rubinfien.
description.extended:
Catalogue of the 2013 Garry Winogrand retrospective, which follows the whole career of Garry Winogrand (1928-1984) and not only the Manhattan street work he is best known for.

Edited by Leo Rubinfien, the book combines plates and short essays by Rubinfien and Erin O'Toole under the headings Down from the Bronx, A Student of America and Boom and Bust. Further essays come from Sarah Greenough, Tod Papageorge and Sandra S. Phillips, O'Toole writes on the problem of editing Winogrand after his death, and Susan Kismaric supplies a chronology. SFMOMA and the National Gallery of Art organized the exhibition, which then traveled to the Metropolitan Museum, the Jeu de Paume in Paris and Fundación MAPFRE in Madrid.

Winogrand did much of his best-known work in Manhattan in the 1960s and also traveled widely across the United States. At his death he left thousands of rolls of undeveloped film and unpublished contact sheets, and the catalogue draws on that archive for photographs not seen before.
